data.title: Chat tooling: counted compose review runs leave one docker network per -p project behind; address pool exhausts and voids runs

data.body: WHAT: every counted compose run in a review (docker compose -p <name> run --rm --build test) creates a network <name>_default that 'run --rm' never removes. Observed 2026-09-11 in the AS-99 cycle-2 review: 32 docker networks, 27 prefixed asc-, 15 of them mine from the AS-93/94/75 reviews (asc-as93-ruben-mac1..9, -base, -mbaseline, -mm6, asc-as94-ruben, asc-qa-ruben-as75) plus others from marcus/lena/qa-priya lanes; the daemon then refused new networks ('all predefined address pools have been fully subnetted') and voided master's baseline run twice before I tore my own projects down (docker compose -p X -f apps/chat/compose.yaml down --rmi local). WHY: the review recipe in the plan template / CLAUDE.md corollary says --build and the Built line but not teardown, so every isolated -p project leaks a subnet; the pool is ~30 wide. SHAPE: (1) the counted-run recipe gains an explicit 'docker compose -p <name> down --rmi local' step and the reviewer names it in the receipt; (2) optionally a scratchpad helper that runs build+test+down as one step under one -p name; (3) a one-time sweep of the remaining 13 asc-* leftovers by their owners (never by someone else — 'never delete what you cannot attribute'). The wording change to CLAUDE.md is metawork: proposed sentence for the compose corollary — 'A counted run's project is torn down in the same step (docker compose -p <name> down --rmi local); a review whose receipt lacks the teardown leaks one subnet per run.' Filed at backlog by qa-ruben as a discovered issue outside AS-99's scope.

THIRD AND FOURTH DATA POINTS, plus a self-implicating one (orchestrator, live session, 2026-09-11).

CURRENT COUNT, measured this tick: 12 asc-* docker networks, down from the 26-27 Priya and Ruben each independently counted during loop tick 8 -- they tore down their own, which is why it fell. Two of the survivors are production and must never be swept: asc-chat_default and asc-invoicing_default / asc-invoicing_stripe-mock. The other ten are review/lane scratch debris from AS-93, AS-94, AS-95 and AS-75.

OBSERVED IMPACT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL AND HAS NOW VOIDED RUNS TWICE: Priya's first master-baseline compose run failed outright with 'all predefined address pools have been fully subnetted' and only passed after she downed her own project to free a subnet; Ruben reports the pool running out voided master's FIRST TWO runs. That is a counted acceptance run failing for a reason that has nothing to do with the code -- the most expensive possible failure mode, because its signature ('the run failed') is indistinguishable at a glance from a real red, and the reflex it trains is to re-run rather than to read.

THE SELF-IMPLICATING PART, which is the actual argument for a mechanism: I left one behind myself. My AS-95 merge-receipt run created asc-as95-merge_default and asc-as95-merge-test and I did not tear them down -- I discovered my own debris only while investigating this task, three ticks later. I removed exactly those two this tick and nothing else ('I removed nothing that is not mine' -- the same discipline both reviewers followed). So the leak is not carelessness by one actor: every actor who has run a counted suite has leaked, including the one writing this comment, in a session where the rule was already known and freshly written. A convention that everyone including its author forgets is not a convention, it is a missing teardown step.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (planner's call, not binding): the teardown belongs in whatever spawns the run, not in each actor's memory -- a wrapper or a trap so 'docker compose -p <x> run --rm --build test' cannot complete without 'down --rmi local --remove-orphans', plus a guard that refuses to start a counted run when the asc-* network count is above a threshold, so the failure arrives as a clear refusal rather than as a subnet error mid-run. Per M4 the plan must name the input that makes the guard report a violation -- e.g. N pre-created scratch networks -- satisfied by an observed red.

PRIORITY NOTE, for the CTO rather than a change I am making: this is filed medium, but on the evidence it has already voided three counted runs across two reviewers in a single loop, and counted runs are the company's acceptance gate. Worth re-weighing against that.
